liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Wharf Rat** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls it the best Wharf Rat ever: delicate, detailed body followed by an explosive jam; The Wharf Rat patch consists of post-song tuning [1][12]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Near seven minutes in at the end of Sugaree, the band plays White Rabbit and talks to someone in the crowd [19]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 other source): The discs have a reel flip in Rider and sporadic anomalies [7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Reviewer highlights the sequence Truckin' into Drums, The Other One, Me & My Uncle, back to The Other One, then Wharf Rat [17]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer says Lovelight swings strongly [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **White Rabbit Tease**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **Bill Graham Announcement**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-08-15.168863.sbd.patched.latvala.miller.menke.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min [1]
- **gd71-08-15.sbd.ladner.21780.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 127 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the audio-board sound and mix, with a strong rhythm section; soundman has occasional problems [13]
- **gd1971-08-15.sbd.gustin.131.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 127 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer notes some recording anomalies and performance flubs; Uploader says this is the best circulating version and sounds amazing despite imperfections [7][15]
- **gd1971-08-15.168862.sonytcd49.menke.miller.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 134 min [2]

## Around the show

- Lineup is stripped down: two guitars, bass, drums and Pigpen on organ; reviewer says the band never sounded like this again [13]
- Reviewer insists Jerry plays a Les Paul here and the previous night, citing photos; says the Stratocaster sound appears at a Gaelic Park show weeks later [14]
- Reviewer says these Berkeley shows match the Hollywood August 5/6 shows in caliber, which circulate only as audience tapes [10]
- Reviewer, who lived in the city, prefers the 15th over the 14th, calling this recording the best of the lot [15]
- Reviewer thinks the August 14 show is better than this one [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-08-15.168863.sbd.patched.latvala.miller.menke.flac1644**: taped by Cassette supplied by Dick Latvala; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 20, 2024; source: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT (44.1k) [1]
- **gd71-08-15.sbd.ladner.21780.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by M. Woyczynski; source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1971-08-15.sbd.gustin.131.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Gustin; source: mSR>cass.>DAT>Serafin digital editing>CDR [7]
- **gd1971-08-15.168862.sonytcd49.menke.miller.flac2496**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Transfer by Bob Menke Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 20, 2024; source: Sony TC-D40 (Built-In Mic) > Cassette Master (TDK 120SD) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-08-14 GD NRPS Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-08-14-gd-nrps-poster/) [21]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1971-08-15 Sun Berkeley Community Theater, Berkeley, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1398804874298/grateful-dead-1971-08-15-sun-berkeley) [22]
